correction.text: the Baja California peninsula, 160,314 km2, for 1853 and 1854 only: the Republic of Lower California from 3 November 1853 and the Baja California part of Walker's Republic of Sonora to 8 May 1854; nothing is drawn for 1855

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria runs the shape to 1855 but the republic ends in 1854 (infobox 'Disestablished: January 21, 1854'; Walker's Sonora presidency ends 8 May 1854 on the Walker page). The page gives no area. The shape is the whole peninsula, which the proclamation claimed ('proclaimed the independence of the peninsula'); the filibusters held only La Paz and Ensenada, so the outline is a claim, not control. Sonora, which the Republic of Sonora named, was never controlled (Walker page) and is not drawn.

correction.text: empty: no land for 1856. This 111,425 km2 outline lies in Nicaragua (bbox lon -87.66 to -83.57, lat 10.70 to 14.81) and is cell for cell the Nicaragua shape of 1853-1859: Walker's presidency of Nicaragua (inaugurated 12 July 1856, resigned 1 May 1857). It belongs to republic-of-nicaragua, which carries a 1856 keyframe; the Republic of Baja California ended in 1854

keyframe_review.note: The Walker page: 'He was inaugurated on July 12, 1856' as president of Nicaragua and 'resign[ed] the presidency of Nicaragua on May 1, 1857'. The Republic of Baja California page says nothing of Nicaragua. Cliopatria uses the Name of Walker's first republic for his Nicaraguan regime.

region.text: La Paz, the territory's capital, taken after the capture of its political head Rafael Espinosa

ledger.note: 3 November 1853: William Walker proclaims the Republic of Lower California at La Paz. 'On November 3, 1853, the mercenaries proclaimed the independence of the peninsula'; the filibusters took La Paz, the territory's capital, after capturing the political head Rafael Espinosa (infobox 'Established: November 3, 1853', capital La Paz, 8,000 inhabitants).

region.text: the Baja California peninsula, claimed by the Republic of Lower California

ledger.note: November 1853: Walker claims the whole peninsula. The proclamation is of 'the independence of the peninsula' (Baja California, 'the larger Republic of Sonora' later); the pages name only La Paz taken and Ensenada held, so the peninsula is the claim and the contest, confidence 2.

21 January 1854: the Republic of Lower California becomes part of Walker's Republic of Sonora. The Baja page infobox ends the Republic of Lower California on 21 January 1854 and says Walker 'declared himself president of the Republic of Sonora' which 'also included Baja California'; the Walker page dates his Sonora presidency 21 January to 8 May 1854 and says Sonora was never controlled. The state and its peninsula continue.

region.text: the Baja California peninsula, last held at Ensenada

ledger.note: 8 May 1854: the end of Walker's Sonora presidency. 'lack of supplies, aridity, and Mexican resistance quickly forced Walker to retreat'; the infobox gives 8 May 1854 as the end of his presidency, and the Baja page has the remnants 'surrendered to the US military in San Diego'. The page gives no day for the retreat itself.

May 1854: the peninsula is Mexican again. No page opened states a Mexican reconquest; the filibuster republic ended with Walker's retreat and surrender (Mexico's dossier dates the return in January 1854, the Baja page infobox's date).

8 May 1854: Walker's republic ends. The infobox of the Walker page closes his presidency of the Republic of Sonora, which included Baja California, on 8 May 1854; he was tried in the US District Court and 'acquitted by the jury' after eight minutes.

wars.name: Walker's filibuster expedition to Baja California and Sonora

zones.text: the Baja California peninsula, La Paz to Ensenada

wars.outcome: The filibusters take La Paz (3 November 1853), move their headquarters to Ensenada, proclaim the Republic of Sonora (21 January 1854) and are forced to retreat by supply, aridity and Mexican resistance; Walker ends his presidency on 8 May 1854, surrenders to the US military in San Diego and is acquitted by the jury at his trial.
wars.note: The page dates only 15 October 1853 (departure), 3 November 1853, 21 January and 8 May 1854; no battle is dated. Sonora, claimed, was never controlled.

certainty.note: A claim over a peninsula of which the filibusters held two towns; no frontier line exists.

notes: Cliopatria's two shapes are the peninsula (1853-1855) and, for 1856, Nicaragua: the second is Walker's presidency of Nicaragua under the wrong Name (verdict wrong; republic-of-nicaragua carries it, with Walker's regimes as renames there). The peninsula shape is the claim; the filibusters held La Paz (Nov 1853) and Ensenada (headquarters) only, and the page opened gives no area. This dossier folds Walker's 'Republic of Sonora' (21 January – 8 May 1854) into the same state as a rename, because the pages say it 'also included Baja California' and Sonora itself was never controlled: no separate Republic of Sonora dossier (listed in other parts' notes as a state Cliopatria lacks) is needed for territory. Dates: Mexico's dossier returns the peninsula in January 1854 (the Baja page's 21 January); this dossier runs the filibuster regime to 8 May 1854 (the Walker page). Not settled: the date of the move to Ensenada, whether the Mexican state retook the peninsula or the filibusters left it, and whether the US Navy forced the retreat (the Baja page is garbled on it). Gazetteer: 'La Paz' (Baja California Sur, Mexico) is not in places.jsonl, only the Bolivian, Argentine and Honduran La Paz; a coordinate stands for it. Page budget: 2 pages, kept.
